analysis: The trial timed out after 1,643.02 allocated GPU-seconds. No validation score was returned, so improvement over the supplied 0.6225 baseline or historical 0.6275 reference is unestablished. The code streams attention through 128 history positions for every candidate chunk and recomputes chunks during backpropagation using activation checkpointing. This bounds tensor sizes but introduces substantial computation and kernel-launch overhead; it is a plausible timeout contributor, not a confirmed cause without execution logs. Diagnostics also perform numerous repeated scoring passes before fitting. The result provides no evidence that training, checkpoint selection, or all four category routes completed.
code_summary: One independently trained LightGCN per category uses supervised-edge masking, prefix-based training, sampled cross-entropy and gated history attention. A zero-initialized, jointly trained candidate projection augments the graph-user attention query, yielding a separate history summary for each candidate while preserving initial baseline scores. Candidate chunks, streamed history attention and activation checkpointing control memory. Training and inference share the scoring helper; the predictor strictly loads one selected checkpoint per category. Diagnostics cover baseline parity, candidate sensitivity, gradients, padding, repeated events, chunk/permutation equivalence and checkpoint reloads. Future work should reduce attention execution overhead within the same single-model architecture before drawing conclusions about recommendation quality.
